queries: WITH r AS (SELECT m.Name, COUNT(*) AS n, 1.0*SUM(t.Bytes)/SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate FROM Track t JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId=t.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.Name), o AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS a FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.rate) AS avg_rate, AVG(r.n) AS avg_track_count, AVG(r.rate - o.a) AS avg_margin_above_overall FROM r CROSS JOIN o WHERE r.rate > o.a

assumptions.assumption: A media type's rate is total Bytes divided by total Milliseconds over its tracks (a ratio of sums), not an average of per-track ratios. Tracks with NULL Bytes add nothing to the byte total but still count in the milliseconds total.

The overall average is the unweighted mean of the per-media-type rates, taken over the media types that have at least one track. Media types with no tracks are excluded because their rate is undefined.
The 'average number of tracks' is the mean of the per-type track counts (all tracks of the type, including those with NULL Bytes) across the qualifying types.

alternatives.interpretation: A media type's rate is the mean of per-track Bytes/Milliseconds ratios, instead of a ratio of totals. Tracks with NULL Bytes are skipped in the rate but still counted in the track count.

assumptions.assumption: A media type's rate is total Bytes divided by total Milliseconds over its tracks (a ratio of sums), not an average of per-track ratios. Tracks with NULL Bytes add nothing to the Bytes total but still add to the Milliseconds total.
Media types are grouped by Name. Media types with no tracks have no rate, so they are left out of the overall simple average.
The overall average is the unweighted mean of the per-media-type rates. The margin is each qualifying type's rate minus that mean, and the result averages those margins.

assumptions.assumption: A media type's rate is its total Bytes divided by its total Milliseconds, taken over its tracks (tracks with NULL Bytes add nothing to the Bytes sum).
The overall average is the simple (unweighted) mean of the per-media-type rates. Only media types that have at least one track are included, because of the inner join.
The track count is the number of tracks per media type. The result is the average of those counts across the media types above the overall average.
